//: The case rows a seeded environment carries, one version of the
shared fixture. `seeds/dev.json` and `seeds/staging.json` name which
of these cases to load, into which firm, opened by which person;
this file says what each case contains.
SHAPE. Every body below is the JSON the API's own routes accept —
a debtor is the PUT /v1/cases/<id>/debtors/<role> body, a collection
item is the POST /v1/cases/<id>/<collection> body — and the loader
parses them with the same core/ functions those routes use, so a
malformed row fails with the API's own field errors and a rule that
tightens (provenance, say) breaks seeding loudly rather than writing
rows the service has stopped agreeing with.
NO IDS ARE PUBLISHED, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. A case's id in an
environment is derived by the loader from the target table, the
firm and this file's `handle`, so two environments seed different
ids from the same fixture and a re-run finds the rows it wrote last
time instead of writing them again. An id written here would be an
id from someone else's environment.
EVERY VALUE IS SYNTHETIC. Nothing here describes a real person, a
real employer or a real account. `seed capture` refuses a source
that is not a dev stack for exactly this reason, and a review of a
diff to this file should ask the same question.
The Chapter 13 case names public payers and agencies as themselves (the
IRS, the Social Security Administration, Florida's reemployment program,
a county court) and real vehicle makes; every person, business, account
and street address in it is invented.
REFERENCES. A case is a graph — a claim names its creditor and its
collateral, a plan names the claims it treats, an income summary names
its debtor — but no id is published, so a fixture names a record by
reference: `{"$ref": "claims/claims-2"}` wherever an id is wanted, and
`"$handle": "claims-2"` on the item it means (`debtors/<role>` for a
debtor). The loader resolves each to the id that record has in the
target before the route's parser sees the body; `seed capture` writes
them. services/admin entrypoints/seed.py, "references".
v1: one Chapter 7 case. v2 (issue 13.12 / #382): its debtor's tax
id, from the Social Security Administration's never-issued advertising
block 987-65-4320..4329 — the only way a real-looking SSN may enter a
fixture; the loader seals it the way the API does.
v3 (milestone 16 staging proof): the two cases milestone 16 (#401, #403,
#406) and the creditor matrix (#404) deferred to a new version. Both were
typed into a dev stack through the API and captured with
`scripts/dev-fixture.sh capture v3`; the tax ids (capture drops them) and
the Chapter 7 sample's two v2 documents were put back by hand.
chapter-7-sample   v2's case, now able to assemble: its creditors carry
city, state and ZIP (so the matrix prints), and it
has a petition and a household size.
chapter-13-sample  a complete above-median Chapter 13 case in M.D. Fla.
(Official Form 113 — not flsb, whose local plan form
the packet refuses): 60-month commitment period, so
B122C-2 files; a saved plan that is feasible and
clears the § 1325(a)(4) test; an assume/reject answer
on every lease. It is the API's own Chapter 13
reference case (services/api tests, test_form_
projections.reference_case_file_chapter_13) with
every name replaced by an invented one.
BOTH PETITIONS PIN expected_filing_date (2026-08-03). The means test's
six-month lookback and the dollar-amounts release are resolved from that
date, else from the case's creation date — and a seeded case is created on
whatever day the seeder runs, so without the pin the pay history would
slide out of the window month by month and the verdict would drift from
above-median to below it. Pinned, the answer is the same on every load.
